tools.name: search_components
tools.description:
Find existing, licence-cleared code (functions, classes, handlers, modules) mined from real
    open-source repositories, before writing it from scratch. Cost: 0 credits (free). Works without
    an API key with a small per-network limit; a free key raises the limits.

    Every result is licence-cl

tools.name: find_similar
tools.description:
Find alternatives to a component you already have: other licence-cleared implementations of
    the same job, to compare scores, licences and stacks. Cost: 0 credits (free; needs a free key).

    Parameters: id (required) -- a component id from search_components. limit -- how many
    (default 8).

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description:
List the function tags (categories) in the library with how many components each has; the
    values search_components accepts as `category`. Cost: 0 credits (free; needs a free key).

    Parameters: limit -- how many tags, most-used first (default 40).

    Returns JSON {"categories": [{"tag": ...

tools.name: get_component
tools.description:
Pull one component's full source code to reuse in the project, with its licence, copyright
    holder, GitHub permalink and an attribution header to keep with the copied code. Cost: 1 credit
    per call (needs a free key; refunded if the id is not available). Re-pulling a component you
    already

tools.name: check_component_security
tools.description:
Check components or repositories for known security advisories before or after you reuse
    them: severity, CVSS, summary and the versions that fix each one. Cost: 0 credits (free; needs a
    free key).

    Advisories are repository-wide: OSV advisories for the packages each repository publishes

tools.name: library_stats
tools.description:
Live size of the library: total licence-cleared components, how many carry full source,
    source repositories, languages and repositories by licence class. Use it to tell the user how
    much is searchable. Cost: 0 credits (free; needs a free key). No parameters.

    Returns JSON counts, refresh

tools.name: list_licenses
tools.description:
List every source repository in the library with its SPDX licence and copyright holder,
    i.e. the NOTICE data behind the attribution on each component. Use it to build a NOTICE file or
    to check a repo's licence. Cost: 0 credits (free; needs a free key). No parameters.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_component_security, get_component_bundle, compose_starter · Private data: search_components, list_licenses, get_component_bundle, compose_starter · Public sink: search_components.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_component_security, get_component_bundle, compose_starter · Private data: search_components, list_licenses, get_component_bundle, compose_starter · Public sink: search_components

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_component_security" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet:
before: "Check components or repositories for known security advisories (CVE/GHSA ids) before or
    after you reuse them. Cost: 0 credits (free; needs a free key).

    Advisories are repository-wide and come from our reputation data, which covers a set of widely
    used repositories: "none_known" means no" → after: "Check components or repositories for known security advisories before or after you reuse
    them: severity, CVSS, summary and the versions that fix each one. Cost: 0 credits (free; needs a
    free key).

    Advisories are repository-wide: OSV advisories for the packages each repository publishes
"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
